entries.appliesTo: operators that make artificial intelligence companions or companion platforms available to users in Oregon

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 1(2) — 'the operator shall provide on the artificial intelligence companion platform a clear and conspicuous notice that indicates that a user is interacting with artificially generated output and not a natural person'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 1(3)(a) — 'unless the operator has a protocol for using evidence-based methods for detecting input from the user that consists of suicidal ideation or intent or self-harm ideation or intent and that prevents the provision of content to the user that encourages suicidal ideation, suicide or self-harm'
dutySources.content-safeguards: § 1(4)(b)(C) — 'does not produce visual representations of sexually explicit conduct or suggest or state that the minor should engage in sexually explicit conduct'; § 1(4)(a)(A) — 'Explicitly claim that the artificial intelligence companion is sentient or human'; § 1(4)(a)(D) — 'Role-play romantic relationships between adults and minors'

sources.scope: § 1(1)(a)(A) — '"Artificial intelligence companion" means a system that uses artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence or algorithms that recognize emotion from input and that are designed to simulate a sustained, human-like platonic, intimate or romantic relationship or companionship with a user'
sources.ageFocus: § 1(3)(a) — 'An operator may not allow users in this state access to an artificial intelligence companion or artificial intelligence companion platform unless the operator has a protocol' (core duties bind as to all users; § 1(4) adds minor-specific duties)
sources.aiDisclosure: § 1(4)(b)(B) — 'Provide a clear and conspicuous reminder at a minimum of every three hours of interaction … along with a further reminder that the user is interacting with artificially generated output'
sources.crisisProtocol: § 1(3)(b)(A) — 'Require an artificial intelligence companion to provide a user that expresses suicidal ideation or intent or self-harm ideation or intent with a referral to and contact information and hyperlink for the national 9-8-8 suicide and crisis lifeline'
sources.breakReminders: § 1(4)(b)(B) — 'a clear and conspicuous reminder at a minimum of every three hours of interaction that the user should take a break from interactions with the artificial intelligence companion'
sources.engagementLimits: § 1(4)(c)(A) — 'Delivering to a user, either on a variable schedule or otherwise, a system of rewards or affirmations with the purpose of reinforcing behavior or maximizing the time during which the user engages with the artificial intelligence companion'
sources.contentSafeguards: § 1(4)(b)(C) — 'does not produce visual representations of sexually explicit conduct or suggest or state that the minor should engage in sexually explicit conduct'
sources.enforcer: § 2(1) — 'An individual who suffers an ascertainable loss of money or property or other injury in fact as a result of an operator's violation of section 1 of this 2026 Act may bring an action in a court of this state'

flags: § 1(3)(c) ('An operator shall publish on the operator's website the details of the operator's protocol') and § 1(5)(a) (annual public report of referral counts and protocol details by December 31 each year) fit no listed duty — the report is posted publicly, not filed with an authority, so incident-reporting/registration-filing do not apply and documentation is limited to models/training data

ageFocus 'all-users' is lossy: § 1(4) imposes additional minor-specific duties (break reminders, sexual-content and manipulation safeguards) when the operator 'knows or has reason to believe' a user is a minor; 'minor' is undefined and no numeric age threshold is stated, so ageThreshold is omitted

aiDisclosure 'periodic' is anchored to the minor-specific three-hour reminder in § 1(4)(b)(B); the general § 1(2) notice duty states no timing and triggers only where a reasonable person would believe they are interacting with a natural person
§ 1(3)(b)(A) permits an alternative youthline referral where the operator identifies the user as under 25 years of age — no fixed param captures this

§ 1(4)(c)(B)-(C) also prohibit guilt/abandonment messaging on attempted disengagement and material misrepresentations about the companion's identity, capabilities or training data (coded under content-safeguards/engagement limits, noted here for completeness)

§ 2(1)(a) statutory damages are 'the greater of the individual's actual damages or statutory damages of $1,000', so actual damages may exceed penaltyMax; § 2(2) allows prevailing-plaintiff attorney fees and costs; § 2(1)(b) allows injunctive relief
